purpose: Second disjoint blind QA sample of exactly 50 Zaporizhzhia canonical alert episodes from the ignored/dark-zone universe, using the Wave 1 selection rules unchanged, to test whether residual strict explosion misses recur outside prior candidate/PPO discovery.

relation_to_wave1.relation: Wave 2 uses the same reconstructed base dark-zone universe and sampling method, then excludes all 50 Wave 1 sampled episode IDs before drawing. No selection rule was changed after seeing Wave 1 outcomes.

methodology.canonical_definition: Episode must be in the frozen Zaporizhzhia denominator; canonical strict and sensitivity episodes are excluded.
methodology.blind_selection: No keyword, source-availability, suspiciousness, or content signal is used to select the 50 episodes.
methodology.randomization: Mulberry32 with seed 20260922; proportional calendar-quarter stratification using floor plus largest remainder; within each quarter episodes are sorted by UTC start and Fisher-Yates shuffled using one deterministic seeded PRNG stream.
methodology.review_search: For each sampled episode, perform a broad independent evidence search across available historical sources, including indexed Telegram archives and official/local/national reporting. Search direct explosion wording and equivalent direct event formulations without using the old explosion candidate generator as a filter.
methodology.timing_controls: Require exact-city evidence and event timing inside the sampled alert, or a source that explicitly states the explosion/strike occurred during that alert. Publication time is not event time. Multiple same-day episodes and cross-midnight cases are checked separately. Air-defence-only wording is not strict explosion evidence.
methodology.replacement_rule: No sampled episode was replaced after content review. No technical-impossibility replacement was needed.
methodology.stop_rule: Review stopped after exactly 50 Wave 2 episodes; no Wave 3 was started.

universe_definition: not in historical explosion review/candidate signal set or its conservative unresolved-date exclusions
not in the reconstructible PPO candidate/pilot set or preserved rejected-lead dates
not among manually checked gap-audit cases
not among already known confirmed strict misses
not among already known needs_review cases
not among any of the 50 Wave 1 blind-sample episodes

stratification.method: proportional by alert_start_date_kyiv calendar quarter; floor plus largest remainder

summary.answer: Wave 2 again found a confirmed strict explosion miss in the dark zone: 1/50. The miss repeats the already known multiple-episodes-same-date/source-discovery pattern rather than introducing a new mechanism.

failure_mechanisms_observed_among_two_bl.note: Mechanisms are multi-label: both positives exhibit both patterns.

combined_wave1_wave2_summary.operational_qa_interpretation: Under the pre-specified scale, 2–3 confirmed misses per 100 is a materially stronger signal that hidden misses are not limited to isolated edge cases; systematic high-recall re-audit should be seriously considered. This is an operational QA interpretation, not a population estimate.
combined_wave1_wave2_summary.ppo_enrichment_interpretation: The two blind waves are descriptively compatible with the hypothesis that PPO/candidate discovery acted as an enrichment filter: the random dark zone has a sparse but nonzero confirmed-miss yield, while previously surfaced PPO/candidate-like material contained a much denser set of false negatives. The 13/51 gap-audit figure is not mechanically comparable to 2/100 because the former denominator is a candidate/source-message set and the blind audit denominator is sampled alert episodes.
combined_wave1_wave2_summary.answer: Across two disjoint blind samples (100 randomly selected ignored Zaporizhzhia alert episodes), 2 confirmed strict explosion misses were found, with 0 additional needs_review. Both misses share the already known multiple-episodes-same-date and source-discovery failure modes.

limitations: The repository does not preserve a literal complete episode-level list for all initial PPO candidate messages. Wave 2 therefore uses exactly the same conservative reconstructible PPO episode/date exclusions as Wave 1; residual overlap with unrecoverable rejected PPO candidates cannot be proven to be zero.
A negative verdict means no qualifying evidence was found in the accessible historical source/search surface; it is not proof that no qualifying source exists anywhere.
Historical source indexing and deleted/edited Telegram material can create source-discovery false negatives.
Publication time is never substituted for event time; this deliberately leaves unresolved cases negative unless the event can be tied to the sampled episode under the existing methodology.
The combined 100-episode blind audit is too small for strong population-rate estimation; the pre-specified operational QA scale is used instead.

Wave 2 is a disjoint without-replacement random sample from the remaining eligible universe. It is an independent selection run operationally, but the two samples are not statistically independent draws with replacement.
